intent: Hold the iteration 1 geometry exactly as the stable base: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m in 12 mm steps, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 m wide by 0.16 m long, mass 0.8 kg. Nothing is changed. I expect the same result as iterations 1 and 6 (score about 324, oval finish rate about 0.70), since the simulator is deterministic for this design. I am not considering any sensor, track or mass change for now. The s-bend and slalom max_error limit is not reachable by geometry under the allowed off-track rule, so any further gain has to come from the controller side or from a different geometry idea that is not yet tested, such as a forward sensor offset (y about 0.06 m), which I would only consider if the Integrator reports the controller cannot reduce s-bend max_error.
learning: Iterations 1 and 6 match exactly, so the simulator is deterministic for a fixed design and controller. Single-race comparisons are therefore reliable for geometry, and the earlier worry about seed luck is resolved. Mass shows a non-monotonic oval finish rate (0.6 kg: 0.30, 0.7 kg: 0.15, 0.8 kg: 0.70), so 0.8 kg is the best-known point and not a smooth optimum. The s-bend and slalom off-track failures come from max_error just above 0.06 m. If the Integrator's controller cannot reduce that, the next geometry hypothesis to test is a forward sensor offset, not further mass or track changes.
rationale: Iteration 6 re-ran the iteration 1 geometry and reproduced its score exactly (324.0661, oval finish 0.70, same per-track metrics). The simulator is therefore deterministic for a fixed design, and the 0.70 oval finish rate is a real property of this geometry, not seed luck. The only other point on the mass axis, 0.7 kg, scored 185.49 (finish 0.15) and 0.6 kg scored 247.82 (finish 0.30), so mass is not a lever to move from 0.8 kg. Every geometry change tested has lowered the score: 16 mm sensors (159.26), wheel_track 0.10 m (175.19), mass 0.6 kg (247.82) and mass 0.7 kg (185.49). The Integrator's feedback sets the rule for this case: if the oval finish rate is about 0.5 or more with oscillation at or below about 0.3, hold this geometry as the stable base. Both conditions hold (finish 0.70, oscillation 0.26). The remaining failures are on the s-bend and slalom, where max_error sits at about 0.064 m, above the 0.06 m off-track limit. The body-width lever cannot raise that limit within the allowed range (0.0125 + 0.18/4 = 0.0575 m, which is still below 0.06 m), so no geometry change I can make here addresses it directly. I therefore keep the iteration 1 geometry unchanged, as the Integrator asked. I did not take the earlier untested ideas (forward sensor offset to y = 0.06 m, or 7 sensors) because they would change the sensing the Integrator has tuned against, and the evidence gives no sign they would help. The expected result is the reference score of about 324.
